rationale:
The defect is a parsing regression in lib/src/parser.dart where long-option name validation rejected underscores: the loop over name.codeUnitAt(i) called _isLetterOrDigitOrHyphen, which only permitted code units for letters, digits, and hyphen (45). The fix replaces that predicate with _isLetterDigitHyphenOrUnderscore, adding code unit 95 (underscore), matching the upstream subject 'Fix parsing: re-allow underscore in long names.' (source_candidate.subject) and the referenced public item dart-archive/args#141, which is in allowed_root_cause_ids and in traceability.verified_fix_issue_numbers. The minimized production patch touches only lib/src/parser.dart and contains exactly two hunks: the call-site predicate swap and the predicate definition; the helper rename is required by the semantic change, not an independent refactor. No test, config, docs, or formatting changes are present in patches/minimized-production.patch, and it is byte-identical to patches/production-fix.patch and to the production half of patches/original-commit.patch. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same commit ('match letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores'), which exercises only pre-existing public API (ArgParser(), addFlag, parse, results[...]) with a name string containing '_' and '-'; it depends on no API introduced by the fix. Strict evidence for both the original and post-minimization runs reports all gates passed, including trigger.buggy_differential with the selector reproducing on the buggy revision, trigger.fixed_clean, trigger.deterministic (3 fingerprint groups), full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers, and full_suite.fixed_all_green over a complete 32-run matrix with 3 repetitions. active_same_project_root_causes is empty, so this underscore-in-long-name validation root cause duplicates no registry entry.

The defect is a single-predicate validation bug in lib/src/parser.dart: long-option name validation rejected underscore code units, so '--some_flag' failed to parse even when registered. The minimized production patch changes exactly that predicate (adds code unit 95) and updates the single call site in the name-validation loop; the helper rename from _isLetterOrDigitOrHyphen to _isLetterDigitHyphenOrUnderscore is semantically required by the behavior change rather than an independent refactor, and the two inline '// Hyphen.'/'// Underscore.' comments sit on the changed lines and match the existing '// Digits.' style. No test, config, or feature-extension content remains in patches/minimized-production.patch, and production_files lists only lib/src/parser.dart. The trigger is the unchanged upstream test from the same fixing commit ('match letters, numbers, hyphens and underscores'), which uses only pre-existing public API (ArgParser, addFlag, parse, results[...]) and exercises a name containing '_' plus '-'; it introduces no API added by the fix, so it is semantically equivalent to the reported defect. Strict machine evidence on the post-minimization revision reports all gates passed: build.both_versions, trigger.buggy_differential with the declared selector failing alone on 7ac64f5, trigger.fixed_clean on 8b6b492, trigger.deterministic across 3 repetitions, and full_suite.buggy_reproduces_only_triggers with no extra failures. active_same_project_root_causes is empty and dart-archive/args#141 is the sole allowed verified issue key, so the root cause is not a duplicate.

No separately filed bug report body text was supplied, so the user-facing symptom description rests on the PR subject 'Fix parsing: re-allow underscore in long names' plus the diff.
The commit subject implies a regression from an earlier commit, but the commit that removed underscore support was not supplied, so the exact regression window is unverified.

The helper rename means any other in-repo reference to _isLetterOrDigitOrHyphen would have to be updated; only the one call site appears in the diff, and no repository-wide search result was supplied to confirm there were no others.
full_suite repetitions is 1, so flaky full-suite behavior outside the isolated trigger is less thoroughly sampled than the 3-repetition trigger matrix.
Analyzer cleanliness was diagnostic only (require_analyze_clean=false), so static-analysis regressions are not gated.
